channel.title: AI Implementation: Governance, Coverage, and Deployment
channel.description: Weekly AI governance, insurance coverage, and senior housing analysis from Ken Leatherman.

item.title: Six Weeks to the Camera Law
item.description: Illinois assisted living residents can install their own cameras starting January 1, 2027. What operators need in writing before the first request.

item.title: The Claim Came First
item.description: The Nvidia board suit shows how fast an oversight claim lands. What senior living boards should ask about D&O and AI before renewal.

item.title: The Enforcer Showed Up Early
item.description: For executives who buy AI tools rather than build them, New York's new AI enforcement unit and California's shutdown recommendations turn your vendors' obligations into leverage you should use now.

item.title: 160 Buildings. 48 Hours. No Pilot.
item.description: A Texas operator put AI in 160 nursing homes in 48 hours with no pilot. The pilot was never the point. Skip it, and something else has to do its job.

item.title: The Policy Now Asks Who Approved It
item.description: Underwriters are starting to ask what your AI agents can do without a human. One carrier just wrote the answer into a policy trigger.

item.title: Delaware Drafted the Unelected Officer
item.description: Delaware is drafting rules for a company an AI agent would run. The authority question it raises is already sitting inside your company.

item.title: Families Are Asking AI About Your Community. Half Who Could Judge Found Errors.
item.description: 70% of families researching senior living use AI. Half of those who could judge found errors. What operators should do about the new front door.

item.title: Your AI Vendor Just Told Its Investors the Insurance May Not Be There
item.description: An AI developer told the SEC the insurance market may not cover a catastrophic AI failure. What CFOs and risk managers should ask their brokers before renewal.

item.title: The Layoff Notice Is Becoming an AI Disclosure
item.description: Connecticut and California now ask layoff notices to address AI. New York's first year shows what a checkbox misses. What employers should log.

item.title: Before Your Community Turns On Ambient AI, Read Your State's Recording Law
item.description: Ambient AI documentation is slated for commercial release in senior care this month. HIPAA won't settle recording consent. Your state's statute might.

item.title: Marsh Says Blanket AI Exclusions Backfire. Carriers Say Their Old Forms Covered Too Much.
item.description: Marsh's CEO warns blanket AI exclusions breed uncertainty. A cyber insurer says why carriers write them. What to ask your broker before renewal.

item.title: Connecticut Printed the Dates. IBM Asked What Boards Did Next.
item.description: Connecticut's AI law is phasing in. IBM found fewer than half of executives changed policy after an AI incident reached the board. Three questions for one meeting.

item.title: AI Is Now the First Salesperson Your Prospects Meet
item.description: Families ask ChatGPT and Gemini about senior living communities before they call. Here is how to audit what AI says about you and who should own the answer.

item.title: "Show Me the Test Results": AI Assurance Becomes an Audit Product
item.description: The AICPA and AIUC now offer a joint SOC 2 plus AIUC-1 certification that live-tests AI agents. What it means for vendor contracts and renewals.

item.title: Colorado Is Defining What "Meaningful Human Review" Actually Means
item.description: Colorado's draft ADMT rules spell out what a meaningful human review must show. Hearing is October 26. What employers should copy now.

item.title: The Alert Can Inform the Nurse. Can It Direct the Aide?
item.description: For skilled nursing and senior living leaders: California's AB 1979 limits how AI can direct frontline staff starting January 1, 2027. Here is what to check before then.

item.title: The Brokers Said No. Your Exclusion Didn't Disappear.
item.description: For risk managers, CFOs, and brokers: Marsh, Aon, and WTW just opposed blanket AI exclusions. That gives buyers leverage at renewal, but it does not remove an exclusion already on the policy.

item.title: The Algorithm Can Flag. A Human Has to Fire.
item.description: For business leaders and boards: California's No Robo Bosses Act bars relying solely on AI for discipline or termination starting July 1, 2027. The human-review standard you build now should work in every state.

item.title: Your Nurses Will Find an AI Tool. The Only Question Is Whose.
item.description: Two operators posted AI results that moved hospitalization and fall rates. Their nurses' warning: give staff tools that work, or they'll find their own.

item.title: Your Underwriter Can Now Find the AI You Didn't Put on the Application
item.description: A new cyber-risk tool lets underwriters scan a company's AI footprint from one domain. The gap between what you disclosed and what you run is about to show.

item.title: Virginia Just Put the Thing AI Runs On Under Review
item.description: Virginia just regulated the power, land, and secrecy behind the data centers AI runs in. It's a governance category most boards haven't opened yet.

item.title: The Camera Points Both Ways
item.description: Senior living operators deploying AI monitoring need a staff-data policy now, or near-miss reporting will quietly dry up.

item.title: Excluded Here. Affirmed There. Covered Nowhere?
item.description: Senior living operators and risk managers face a split AI insurance market where the same failure can be excluded on one line and affirmed on another.

item.title: The Algorithm Doesn't Get the Last Word
item.description: Employers, senior living operators included, need a named human behind automated job decisions as Connecticut's AI law phases in and state enforcers line up.

item.title: Nobody Owns Your AI. Hire Someone Who Does.
item.description: Senior living operators who keep adding AI tools without a named owner for adoption are building exposure, not capacity, and the leaders pulling ahead have already fixed it.

item.title: Silence Isn't Coverage.
item.description: Risk managers and CFOs who assume their AI is insured because nothing in the policy excludes it are holding the most common, and least tested, position in the market.

item.title: The Off-Switch Test.
item.description: Board members and executives in any industry should be able to answer the question two governors just asked AI labs: if this system does harm, who can stop it, and how fast?

item.title: Adoption Outran Accounting
item.description: Nursing home AI enthusiasm hit an eight-year high. A quarter of leaders can't name a category where it paid. What to measure before you buy anything else.

item.title: Your Carrier Already Ran Your AI Due Diligence
item.description: State regulators approved more than 80% of carrier requests to exclude AI damages. Your renewal is not a negotiation about a proposal. Four questions to ask now.

item.title: California Built the Auditor. Your Vendor Has No Certificate.
item.description: California just built the first state framework for independent AI verification. It changes what counts as knowing your AI works, in any industry.
